description: Four D latches on a common clock: each output either follows its own input or holds the level that input had when the clock last changed.

inputs.text: The level that latch follows while it is transparent, and holds on to when it is not.
Together with POLARITY this sets when the latches are transparent: they follow their inputs while this jack and POLARITY are at the same level, and hold while the two differ.
Reverses which half of the clock the latches are transparent on: with this low they follow their inputs while CLOCK is low, with this high they follow while CLOCK is high.

outputs.text: 10V while that latch holds a high, 0V while it holds a low.
The inverse of that latch: 10V while the latch holds a low.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
With nothing patched into CLOCK or POLARITY both count as low, which makes all four latches transparent, so the outputs follow the inputs until a clock is patched.
